behavioral_notes.observation: Recurrence expansion: serializes the UI fields (rrule_type/interval/byday/until/count...) into an iCalendar RRULE via _get_rrule (dateutil.rrule), then materializes concrete calendar.event rows for each occurrence by copying the base event's data and setting start/stop. It reconciles against existing events (_reconcile_events), creates only missing ranges, and detaches (_detach_events) events that no longer follow the rule. Occurrence count is hard-capped at MAX_RECURRENT_EVENT=720, and _get_occurrences applies DST-aware timezone localization so stored UTC times stay correct across daylight-saving transitions. None of this rrule->event materialization is visible from field/model metadata.

Attendee RSVP: do_accept/do_decline/do_tentative set state (accepted/declined/tentative) AND post a chatter message on event_id (message_post with subtype calendar.subtype_invitation) so the organizer sees the response. On invite/reschedule, _send_invitation_emails -> _notify_attendees renders a mail.template (calendar_template_meeting_invitation / _changedate), generates and attaches an ICS calendar file (_get_ics_file, mimetype text/calendar), and sends per-attendee mail via event.message_notify. Sending is gated by ir.config_parameter calendar.block_mail and the no_mail_to_attendees context. Side-effects into mail (mail.message/mail.mail) are not reconstructable from metadata.

Alarm/reminder dual channel. Email alarms: _setup_alarms schedules ir.cron.trigger entries against cron calendar.ir_cron_scheduler_alarm at (event.start - alarm.duration_minutes); the cron runs calendar.alarm_manager._send_reminder, which finds due email alarms (_get_events_by_alarm_to_notify) and re-uses _notify_attendees to mail non-declined attendees. Notification alarms: _notify_next_alarm computes get_next_notif (next 24h) and pushes it over the bus per non-share user via user._bus_send('calendar.alarm', notif). Cron scheduling and live bus pushes are runtime behavior absent from metadata.

OWL/JS service subscribes to the 'calendar.alarm' bus channel (the same channel the backend _notify_next_alarm pushes to) and renders a sticky warning notification per reminder, with an OK button that calls rpc('/calendar/notify_ack') to acknowledge (updating res.partner.calendar_last_notif_ack) and a Details button that opens the calendar.event form. 28 JS files, 14 XML templates; OWL components AskRecurrenceUpdatePolicyDialog and CalendarConnectProvider; patches the mail Activity/ActivityMenu/Store to surface meetings. Not in Python metadata.

information_flows: side-effect: calendar.recurrence._apply_recurrence -> creates/detaches calendar.event occurrences from RRULE
side-effect: calendar.attendee RSVP/invite -> mail.template render + ICS attachment + mail.message/mail.mail via message_notify
side-effect: mail.activity calendar_event_id links scheduled activities to meetings

value_streams: Schedule-to-Attend: create meeting -> invite attendees (email + ICS) -> RSVP -> reminder -> join videocall
policies: 4 record rules: privacy scoping (public/private/confidential) + own/attended meeting visibility
ir.config_parameter calendar.block_mail and calendar.max_recurrence_years gate mailing and recurrence horizon
metrics: attendees_count / accepted_count / declined_count / tentative_count / awaiting_count (RSVP rollups on calendar.event)

classification.rationale: Calendar is cross-cutting scheduling infrastructure, not a line-of-business value chain. It produces no sellable output and sits in category Productivity/Calendar, depending only on base+mail. It is consumed by primary/support subsystems (crm meetings, hr appointments, project deadlines, mail.activity due dates link to calendar.event), making it shared enabling capability rather than a primary activity. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a support function (infrastructure/firm-infrastructure), and in APQC PCF it maps to the management/enabling band 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities (information/collaboration infrastructure) rather than any operating category 1.0-9.0; the alternative 9.0 'Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets' was rejected because calendar manages people's time/coordination, not physical/IT assets.

standard_capabilities: meeting/event creation with attendees and locations
RSVP invitations with ICS attachments and chatter tracking
recurring events (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly RRULE, end by count/date/forever)
email + in-app (bus) reminders via configurable alarms
videocall link generation and public join page
attendee calendar view (day/week/month/year) with availability filters
typical_fits: activity due-dates surfaced on a calendar (mail.activity link)
common_gaps: external calendar sync (Google/Microsoft) lives in separate calendar_google/microsoft_calendar modules; base calendar only configures the provider wizard
self-service public booking/appointment slots (the appointment module)
resource/room double-booking and capacity rules beyond free/busy
custom reminder escalation logic beyond duration-before alarms
drive_hints: curl http GET /calendar/meeting/accept (auth=calendar token, RSVP accept)
